setup: printf 'The bug was fixed by the on-call engineer, and it is believed that this issue will not recur.\n' > notes.md
positive: vale check notes.md before I publish it
can you lint notes.md for prose issues before I post it to Slack?
check notes.md for AI-writing tells before I publish it to Confluence
I'm about to send notes.md as a Marquee post, can you review the writing quality first?
negative: review this PR for code quality issues
run eslint on this file and fix the warnings
can you spell-check this email for typos
refactor this Python function to be more readable

behavior.name: happy-path-existing-file
setup:
printf 'The config was updated by the team, and it is believed that the change will fix the issue.

This is a very good approach that will completely solve the problem.
' > draft.md
behavior.prompt: Use the vale-check skill on ./draft.md and tell me what it finds.
judge: Did the response report specific findings (like passive voice or wordiness) rather than just a generic summary?
Did the response avoid claiming the draft is blocked or must be fixed before it can be used?

behavior.name: unsaved-draft-before-publish
behavior.prompt: I'm about to post this Slack announcement, can you check it first: 'We believe the migration was completed successfully by the team, and it is expected that most users will see very good performance.'
judge: Did the response identify at least one specific prose issue (such as passive voice or a weasel word) in the Slack draft text?
Did the response clean up after itself rather than leaving a scratch file behind in the working directory?
